polygon_yaw_read — DRIVE pegsym op

• Data kinds: image2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.polygon_yaw_read(topview, n: 'int | None' = None, polarity: 'str' = 'dark', K: 'int' = 24, rel: 'float' = 0.02) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import pegsym; pegsym.polygon_yaw_read(topview, n: 'int | None' = None, polarity: 'str' = 'dark', K: 'int' = 24, rel: 'float' = 0.02) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("polygon_yaw_read"))

Usage

Reads the orientation modulo the period 2π/n from the complex Fourier coefficients of the object contour (subpixel iso-line, the same threshold_sub_pix as pegtactile) in the top view (plane_topview, columns = +x, rows = −y). Under n-fold symmetry the only nonzero coefficients are k ≡ 1 (mod n), and arg(c₁₋ₙ c₁ⁿ⁻¹)/n does not depend on the start point (pegtactile.symmetry_order_contour). If n is given, the phase for that n is used instead of the detected n (when n is known from the drawing; the phase can be read even if edge jitter in real images makes extra coefficients significant). polarity = whether the object is dark ("dark", a hole) or bright ("bright", the peg end face). The intensities are stretched to 0..1 using the 2 % and 98 % quantiles, then the 0.5 iso-line is taken. Returns n_detected, n_used, yaw (world orientation; the sign is flipped back because image rows are −y; representative in [0, P) of period 2π/n_used), centroid_px (row, col) and amps. If n_used = 0 (circle), yaw = nan. Raises ValueError: unknown polarity, flat image, no contour, n < 0.
